introduction:
House and Land Documents typically refer to Property Registration, which is a mandatory process governed by the Registration Act, 1908. Registering your property ensures legal ownership and protects against disputes in Telangana.

The registration process involves paying stamp duty and registration fees, and must be completed at the local Sub-Registrar's Office within 4 months of the execution of the sale deed. It serves as an undeniable record of title and rights over the property.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Official Portals:
    • Non-Agricultural (Urban/Housing): IGRS
    • Agricultural Land: Bhu Bharati (Note: Replaced the Dharani portal in April 2025, though many still refer to it as Dharani).
  • Total Cost: Approx. 6% to 7.5% of the property market value.
    • Stamp Duty: ~4-5%
    • Transfer Duty: ~1.5%
    • Registration Fee: 0.5%
  • Processing Time: Registration is often completed on the same day as the SRO visit; documents are downloadable within 24-48 hours.
  • Mandatory Rule: You cannot walk into a Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) without an online appointment (slot booking).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Property Registration

Requirement: You must have original hard copies and scanned soft copies of the following documents.
Required for All Properties
  • Sale Deed: A drafted document containing details of the sale, boundaries, and transaction value.
  • Encumbrance Certificate (EC): Proof that the property is free from legal dues/mortgages.
  • Identity Proofs: Aadhaar Card and PAN Card for Buyer, Seller, and two Witnesses.
  • Photos: Passport-size photos of Buyer and Seller.
  • Section 32A Form: A form with photos and thumb impressions of executants and witnesses.
  • Payment Receipts: Challan/receipt for Stamp Duty and Registration fees paid online.
Specific to Agricultural Land (Bhu Bharati/Dharani)
  • Pattadar Passbook: The seller's digital or physical passbook.
  • Succession/Mutation Documents: If applicable.
Specific to Non-Agricultural (IGRS)
  • Property Tax Receipt: Latest receipt to prove tax compliance.
  • Market Value Certificate: To verify the government rate for stamp duty calculation.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Registration & Slot Booking (Mandatory Stage)

You must complete the online stage on the respective portal depending on your property type to secure an SRO/Tahsildar appointment.

A. For Non-Agricultural Property (House, Plot, Flat) via IGRS
  1. Create Login: Visit the IGRS Telangana Portal and create a user ID.
  2. Public Data Entry (PDE): Select the "Public Data Entry" option. Enter details of the property (Survey No., extent, boundaries) and the parties involved (Buyer/Seller info).
  3. Upload Documents: Upload the drafted Sale Deed, EC, and ID proofs as PDF/JPEG.
  4. Pay Charges: Use the fee calculator to find the Stamp Duty. Pay the amount online via net banking/UPI/challan generation. Save the E-Challan receipt.
  5. Book Slot: Select "Slot Booking." Choose your jurisdictional Sub-Registrar Office (SRO), date, and time. You will receive a Slot Booking Reference Number and an SMS confirmation.
B. For Agricultural Land via Bhu Bharati (formerly Dharani)
  1. Visit Portal: Go to bhubharati.telangana.gov.in.
  2. Select Service: Choose "Slot Booking for Citizen" followed by the transaction type (e.g., "Sale").
  3. Enter Details: Input the Passbook number or Survey number to fetch land details automatically.
  4. Verification: The system validates ownership. Proceed to pay stamp duty online.
  5. Book Appointment: Select a slot at the local Tahsildar (MRO) office.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Physical Visit to SRO/Tahsildar (Slot Booking Required)

Note: Purely "offline" applications without online slot booking are no longer standard. You must book a slot online first.
On the Day of Appointment:
  1. Arrive Early: Reach the Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) or Tahsildar office 15 minutes before your slot.
  2. Check-in: Show your Slot Booking Reference SMS/printout at the counter. An officer will generate a "Check Slip" based on your online data.
  3. Verify Check Slip: Review the Check Slip carefully for spelling errors in names or survey numbers. Correct them immediately if found.
  4. Biometrics (E-KYC): The Buyer, Seller, and Witnesses will be called to give thumb impressions and have photos taken via the official webcam. This is verified against the Aadhaar database.
  5. Submission: Hand over the physical Sale Deed and original documents to the Registrar.
  6. Approval: The Registrar signs and approves the registration. You will be given a document receipt.
afterApplying:
After Applying — Document Collection & Mutation

1. Document Scanning

The SRO officials will scan the signed Sale Deed for digital records.

2. Collection Details
  • Agricultural Land: The mutation is often instant or updated within a week in the Bhu Bharati digital records. You can download the new e-Passbook online.
  • Non-Agricultural Property: The registered Sale Deed is usually ready for collection on the same day or available for download from the IGRS portal within 24-48 hours.
3. Post-Registration Mutation

Ensure you apply for Mutation (name change in municipal/revenue records) at your local municipal office if it wasn't auto-processed.
